hints: Focus on just the ester linkage, the $\text{-O-C(=O)-}$ group, and ignore the rest of the large molecule for now.
Look at the acyl side of that ester, the $\text{C(=O)}$ carbon is joined directly to an $\text{H}$ atom.
Remember acid hydrolysis splits the ester into an alcohol plus the carboxylic acid from the acyl fragment, so ask what $\text{H-C(=O)-OH}$ molecule that gives.
walkthrough:
**Spot the ester linkage**

Look for the $\text{-O-C(=O)-}$ pattern. In this molecule it is on the top right as $\text{-O-C(=O)-H}$.

General hydrolysis:
$$\text{R-O-C(=O)-R' + H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{R-OH + R'-C(=O)-OH}$$

**Split the ester correctly**

The single bond between the O and the $\text{C=O}$ carbon breaks. The O stays with the big ring to give an alcohol, and the $\text{C=O}$ fragment picks up $\text{OH}$ to give the acid.

Here the split is:
$$\text{ring-O-H + H-C(=O)-OH}$$

**Identify the small acid**

The acyl group is $\text{H-C(=O)-}$, just one carbon with an H attached. Adding $\text{OH}$ gives $\text{H-C(=O)-OH}$.

That is methanoic acid, also called formic acid, $\text{HCOOH}$, which is a very simple one-carbon acid.

options.A: Correct. The ester is a methanoate (formate) ester, $\text{R-O-CHO}$. Acid hydrolysis gives $\text{HCOOH}$, methanoic acid, shown as $\text{H-C(=O)-OH}$.
options.B: Incorrect. This shows a large opened-chain hydroxy-acid. It wrongly assumes the ring ether and ketone also hydrolyse, but acid hydrolysis under these conditions only cleaves the ester linkage.
options.C: Incorrect. This keeps the whole ring attached to a $-\text{O-C(=O)-OH}$ group. That would come from adding $\text{CO}_2$, not from splitting an existing $\text{-O-CHO}$ ester.
options.D: Incorrect. This is a large keto-acid with a different ester still present. It confuses which side of the ester becomes the acid and wrongly opens the ring.
